nodes.name: Liquid-phase IH synthesis of NiMoO4/NF-IH
nodes.procedure: 75 mL homogeneous solutions composed of 1 mmol NiCl2·6H2O and 1 mmol Na2MoO4·2H2O were transferred into a 50 mL vessel. The 1 cm × 4 cm NF was cleaned in 3M HCl for 15 min with ultrasonication and then washed to neutral with deionized water and ethanol. A piece of precleaned NF rolled and fixed on a glass tube was placed inside the vessel, which was put in the middle of induction coils composed of three copper loops with an inner diameter of 60 mm. The operating current generated by an induction apparatus was set at 30 A. The NF was heated for 3 min under atmospheric open system conditions. Then the yellow-green NiMoO4 nanowires grown on the NF (NiMoO4/NF-IH) was obtained, rinsed with deionized water and ethanol several times, and finally dried at room temperature.

unit_operations.name: NF Cleaning
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The 1 cm × 4 cm NF was cleaned in 3M HCl for 15 min with ultrasonication and then washed to neutral with deionized water and ethanol.

nodes.name: Liquid-phase IH synthesis of NiFe LDH/NF-IH
nodes.procedure: A piece of precleaned NF (1 cm × 4 cm) was rolled and fixed on a glass tube, then immersed in 15 mL solution containing 25×10^-3 M Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 25×10^-3 M Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 0.2 M NH4F, and 0.7 M CO(NH2)2 with stirring for 10 min to achieve homogeneity. This solution with NF was transferred to a 50 mL vessel which was placed in induction coils. The NF was heated for 3 min in the above solution with operation current (30 A) generated by induction apparatus. After cooling for about 10 min, the sample was taken out, washed with deionized water and ethanol, and dried in air.

nodes.name: Gas-phase IH reduction to Ni-MoO2/NF-IH
nodes.procedure: The as-synthesized NiMoO4/NF-IH was rolled and fixed on a glass tube and then placed inside the vessel which was located in the middle of induction coils. The sample was heated for 2 min with an operating current of 25 A under 100 sccm Ar-H2 (10%) flow. After cooling naturally, the Ni nanoparticles anchored on MoO2 nanowires/NF (Ni-MoO2/NF-IH) was taken out and used for material characterizations and electrochemical performance tests directly.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMoO4/NF-IH shows abundantly interconnected nanowires randomly grown on NF surface with diameter 50–70 nm and length >500 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the abundantly interconnected NiMoO4 nanowires randomly grew on the surface of NF with a diameter of 50–70 nm and a length of more than 500 nm, as observed by SEM images in Figure 2a.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMoO4/NF-IH exhibits weak crystallinity and porous structure with interplanar distance of 0.299 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The weak crystallinity and porous structure of NiMoO4 were confirmed by transmission electron microscopic (TEM) images in Figure 2b,c.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMoO4/NF-IH shows clear interplanar distance of 0.299 nm in single nanowire with abundant dislocations and distortions indicating defective structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The clear interplanar distance of 0.299 nm in a single NiMoO4 nanowire was detected by high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) in Figure 2c... abundant dislocations and distortions could be observed from Figure 2c, indicating defective structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS element mapping shows Mo, Ni, and O elements uniformly distributed in NiMoO4 nanowire.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) element mapping in Figure 2d shows that the Mo, Ni, and O elements were distributed uniformly in NiMoO4 nanowire.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH/NF-IH composed of many nanosheets with thickness ~20 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of NiFe LDH/NF-IH was composed of many nanosheets with the thickness of about 20 nm, which was confirmed by SEM images (Figure 2e).
which was confirmed by SEM images (Figure 2e) and TEM image (Figure 2f).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH/NF-IH shows few unclear lattice fringes with interlayer spacing of 0.25 nm, weak crystallinity, and defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Figure 2g, only a few unclear lattice fringes with an interlayer spacing of 0.25 nm were detected, implying the weak crystallinity of NiFe LDH... a few defects could be observed in Figure 2g.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping indicates homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, and O elements in NiFe LDH/NF-IH nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding EDS mapping in Figure 2h indicates that the homogeneous distribution of Ni, Fe, and O elements in overall NiFe LDH/NF-IH nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMoO4/NF-IH shows Ni 2p1/2 at 874.4 eV and Ni 2p3/2 at 856.5 eV with satellite peaks; Mo 3d5/2 at 232.1 eV and Mo 3d3/2 at 235.2 eV indicating Mo6+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Ni 2p1/2 and Ni 2p3/2 peaks of NiMoO4/NF-IH are situated in 874.4 and 856.5 eV, respectively, accompanied with two satellite peaks. The high-resolution Mo 3d signal... Mo 3d5/2 (232.1 eV) and Mo 3d3/2 (235.2 eV), showing... Mo6+.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe LDH/NF-IH shows Ni 2p3/2 at 856.1 eV, Ni 2p1/2 at 873.9 eV with satellites at 861.8 and 880.1 eV; Fe 2p3/2 at 712.4 eV, Fe 2p1/2 at 725.4 eV with satellites indicating Fe3+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The two peaks of Ni 2p, Ni 2p3/2, and Ni 2p1/2, were located at 856.1 and 873.9 eV, respectively, along with their shake-up satellite peaks at 861.8 and 880.1 eV. The Fe 2p peak was composed of Fe 2p3/2 and Fe 2p1/2 located at 712.4 and 725.4 eV... implying... Fe3+.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-MoO2/NF-IH shows nanowires with rough porous surface and nanoparticles emerging from nanowire surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of nanowires still retained while the surface became rough and porous. Meanwhile, a large number of nanoparticles emerged from the surface of nanowires, as observed by SEM (Figure 3a).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-MoO2/NF-IH confirms nanowire morphology with nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: as observed by SEM (Figure 3a) and TEM (Figure 3b) images.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-MoO2/NF-IH shows MoO2 (111) plane at 0.24 nm, Ni (111) plane at 0.2 nm, and defects due to dislocations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM image in Figure 3c shows a clear lattice fringe with an interplanar distance of 0.24 nm on the nanowire, which was assigned to the (111) plane of MoO2. The other lattice fringe with an interplanar distance of 0.2 nm (Figure 3d) was well-matched with the (111) plane of Ni... some defects could be observed in Figure 3e (marked with red lines).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows Mo and O mainly in nanowires, Ni mainly in nanoparticles confirming Ni-MoO2 heterostructure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the distribution of Mo, Ni, and O elements was illustrated by the EDS mapping, where Mo and O elements were mainly distributed in the nanowires, but Ni element was mainly lied in part of nanoparticles (Figure 3f), confirming the heterostructure.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMoO4/NF-IH shows weak diffraction peaks at 27.3° and 29.8° indexed to NiMoO4·xH2O (JCPDS no. 13-0128); NiFe LDH/NF-IH shows no obvious diffraction peaks except NF characteristic peaks, implying weak crystallization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the diffraction peaks located at 44.5°, 51.8°, and 76.3° were indexed to... Ni... The other two weak diffraction peaks emerged at 27.3° and 29.8°, which was well-indexed to NiMoO4·xH2O (JCPDS no. 13-0128). The XRD pattern of NiFe LDH/NF-IH... shows no obvious diffraction peaks of NiFe LDH except the characteristic peaks of NF, implying the weak crystallization.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-MoO2/NF-IH shows Ni peaks at 44.5°, 51.8°, 76.3° and MoO2 peaks at 26.0°, 36.7°, 53.0° confirming metallic Ni and monoclinic MoO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Comparing to NiMoO4/NF-IH, the XRD investigation also clearly verified that the Ni-MoO2 consisted of metallic Ni and monoclinic MoO2. As shown in Figure 3g, apart from three diffraction peaks of 44.5°, 51.8° and 76.3° corresponding with Ni (JCPDS No.04-0850), the others appearing at 26.0°, 36.7°, and 53.0° were assigned to MoO2 (JCPDS No. 32-0671).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-MoO2/NF-IH Mo 3d deconvoluted to Mo4+ (229.4 eV), Mo5+ (230.3 eV), Mo6+ (232.3 eV); Ni 2p3/2 (856.1 eV), 2p1/2 (873.8 eV) with satellites; metallic Ni0 2p3/2 (852.6 eV), 2p1/2 (870.0 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-resolution Mo 3d signal of Ni-MoO2 could be deconvoluted into three typical components with binding energy located at 229.4, 230.3, and 232.3 eV, corresponding to Mo4+, Mo5+, and Mo6+... The high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum... was deconvoluted to 856.1 and 873.8 eV accompanying with two satellite peaks... The Ni0 2p3/2 peaks at 852.6 eV and the Ni0 2p1/2 peaks at 870.0 eV were assigned to metallic Ni.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-MoO2/NF-IH shows charge transfer resistance Rct of 3.3 Ω at 300 mV overpotential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni-MoO2/NF-IH exhibited the smaller Rct value of 3.3 Ω at the overpotential of 300 mV than NF (12.6 Ω) and NiMoO4/NF (7.12 Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-MoO2/NF-IH double-layer capacitance Cdl = 21.6 mF cm-2 indicating high electrochemical surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the double-layer capacitance values (Cdl) of Ni-MoO2/NF-IH was calculated to 21.6 mF cm-2, which was higher than NF (0.74 mF cm-2), NiMoO4/NF-IH (1.42 mF cm-2).
